newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries steady in London, focus on auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady in London, focus on auction.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries traded in London were holding firm on Wednesday as investors are waiting to see how new supply is absorbed, traders said.
The U.S. Treasury will auction $12.5 billion of five-year notes later in the session, following the auction of $17 billion of two-year notes on Tuesday.

"Yesterday's auction was quite well-absorbed, but there's a feeling of wanting to get it out of the way before committing mush more money to this market," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "Since there isn't any data, people are comfortable sitting where they are."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was trading at 94-25, yielding 7.045 percent, compared with 94-24 in Tokyo and 94-26 at the New York close.

Analysts said the absence of key data was bringing any comments by Federal Reserve bankers into the limelight. Comments by Richmond Fed president Alfred Broaddus, who said the U.S. economy was strong, were watched carefully, they said.

"For him, it was a bland speech, since he tends to be hawkish," said Andrew Davies, bond analyst at the London Bond Broking Company here. "You could draw the inference that he is less likely to push for a rate rise next time."
Davies said he did not expect the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its May meeting, as the effects of the March rise would have had little time to filter through into the economy.
He said the market would look for indications of rate policy from Chicago Fed president Michael Moskow, who is speaking at a Chicago Federal Reserve Bank symposium on the midwest economy at 1430 GMT.
Davies said there could be a small rally after the supply, but he saw strong resistance at the 7.0 percent yield level in the short-term.
June T-bond futures were up 6/32 at 108-10 in automated trade. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
